findings.passage: “People do inadvertently get registered to vote,” Wesco said. “It’s frankly doing them a favor to make sure that they are taken off the voter registration rolls, because when they apply for citizenship, (the registration) can become a problem for them in that process.”
findings.note: Quoted by The Indiana Citizen in its report on the House debate on HB 1264 (2024). Date is the article date; the floor remarks were that week. Defends checking registrations against records to find non-citizens on the voter rolls.

The Indiana Citizen (a news report, not the official bill page, which did not load) calls him the author of HB 1264. Per that report the bill compares voter registrations to Bureau of Motor Vehicles records and federal jury forms to identify non-citizens, and lets the Secretary of State verify addresses with commercially available data. The report says he said the bill is not anti-immigrant.
